memory_envelope.correction_2026_08_28: The single cycle_peak_over_live_max=1.8 entry conflated two independent §1.3 rows that share no numerator, denominator, or sampling point: allocator-side quiescent committed/live < 1.3, and collector-pacing cycle peak/live < 1.8. gate_smoke.sh's committed/live column measures the FORMER; comparing it against 1.8 crosses metrics and was driver error. Two consequences. (1) A raw committed/live ratio is a bad small-heap gate: it charges a whole 2 MiB superblock against live bytes, so deltablue reads 12.04x purely from 2,097,152/141,200 granularity, and C/L_block diverges as live -> 0 even with retained capacity under one superblock. Replaced by an absolute fixed-plus-scaled envelope. (2) 'P/S < 1.8' is self-contradictory under the implemented threshold T = max(1.75*S, S + 1.5MiB): on the floor arm T/S = 1 + 1.5MiB/S already exceeds 1.8 for S < 1.875 MiB with zero overshoot, and is unbounded as S -> 0. Expressing the gate against the selected threshold as P/T < 36/35 = 1.8/1.75 exactly retains the growth-arm decision while staying meaningful on the floor arm. A rounded 1.03 would permit P/S = 1.8025 and is not a faithful hard gate; 1.025 leaves measurement margin. Measured cycle overshoot in the splay probe was P/T = 1.000031 (7,899 bytes), so the previously reported 4.63x was denominator-scope mismatch, not overshoot. This is a definitional correction, not a loosening: the growth-arm decision is unchanged. Derivation by lane-f, docs/tracing-gc-pause-plan.md.

activation_canary.rule: Per-workload minimum mechanism coverage. Thresholds are derived, not hand-picked: for each GC-heavy workload, minimum_major_cycles_per_sample, minimum marked/allocated bytes, minimum swept bytes, and minimum gc_active_time_share are frozen at 0.5x the values recorded by the candidate arm in the GC-GAP evidence manifest, automatically, when that manifest lands. A gate sample failing any canary row is invalid (not a pass, not a fail).
categorical_requirements: each GC-heavy workload independently triggers at least one major collection per sample
collector mode and policy digest identical across all samples
growth factor identical across measurement/test/release configurations
measurement, test, and release configurations run the same collector code (no builtin.is_test divergence)
activation_canary.census_exclusion_note_2026_08_29: The 'pause timer excludes census/reporting time' row was satisfied on the whole-STW path from the start (runtime.zig subtracts last_census_ns in the CollectionResult duration blk) but NOT on the incremental path: from dd768214 (2026-08-28), recordFinalMarkFootprint ran a whole-heap census inside finishIncrementalCycle's t_remark..t_weak window with no deduction, so the path that actually runs reported an inflated pause from the same --gc-stats flag that printed the distribution. The incremental path satisfies this canary row as of 7e233ccb (2026-08-29), which moved the census behind its own --gc-mark-footprint flag and added the missing deduction. Consequence for gate inputs: any tracing pause number captured with --gc-stats on a build in the dd768214..7e233ccb range is invalid and may not be used as a canary or benefit reading. Readings from before dd768214 (including the GC-GAP evidence) are NOT affected -- verified against 62061f94's sources, see reports/evidence/GC-GAP/ERRATA-2026-08-29.md.
activation_canary.basis: doc (roadmap §2 canary list); derivation constant 0.5x is proposed
